- If sentiment is consistently low or neutral in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or shift downward.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% in 3-5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast growth or introduce early mean-reversion logic.
- When sentiment shows increasing pessimism (e.g., >2/3 negative or declining), model should adjust downward, especially if recent price action is volatile or declining.
- If model shows strong upward trend over 30d but true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 10-15d peak then drop), reduce forecast slope after 10-12d.
- If sentiment is high but price drops sharply (e.g., >3% in 1-2d), model may overreact; add buffer zone or reduce forecast magnitude for next 3-5d.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is mixed or neutral, model should not assume linear growth; introduce volatility decay or smoothing factor.
